title: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart
body:
Read the chapter → [Joshua 5](/bible/joshua/5)

## Introduction

This session covered [Joshua 5](/bible/joshua/5) through 8: the circumcision of the wilderness generation at Gilgal and what the uncircumcised heart means, the Captain of the host of the Lord, the fall of Jericho and the faith of Rahab, the accursed thing and the sin of Achan, the taking of Ai, and the blessings and cursings read at mount Ebal. By way of recap of chapters 1 through 4: after the death of Moses, Joshua was set over the host of Israel, the Lord dried up the river Jordan so the people crossed on dry ground, and the spies Joshua sent had linked up with Rahab the harlot in Jericho. Rahab worked as counterintelligence for Israel; she dwelt on the side of the wall in the poor quarter of the city, and such people know the secret goings-on of a city, so she gave the spies information to carry back to Joshua.

**[Joshua 5:1](/bible/joshua/5#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/joshua/5#v1)</sup> And it came to pass, when all the kings of the Amorites, which were on the side of Jordan westward, and all the kings of the Canaanites, which were by the sea, heard that the Lord had dried up the waters of Jordan from before the children of Israel, until we were passed over, that their heart melted, neither was there spirit in them any more, because of the children of Israel.

- The kings of the Amorites and the Canaanites heard that the Lord had dried up the waters of Jordan from before the children of Israel, and their heart melted: they were paralyzed with fear.
- They had heard how the Most High split the Red sea in Exodus, and now he had done it again at Jordan, so neither was there spirit in them any more because of the children of Israel.

**[Joshua 5:2-3](/bible/joshua/5#v2)**

> <sup>[2](/bible/joshua/5#v2)</sup> At that time the Lord said unto Joshua, Make thee sharp knives, and circumcise again the children of Israel the second time.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/joshua/5#v3)</sup> And Joshua made him sharp knives, and circumcised the children of Israel at the hill of the foreskins.

- Circumcise again the children of Israel the second time: the children of Israel had not been keeping the commandments, being stiffnecked and hardheaded, and the Lord told Joshua to fix them.
- Circumcision is the covenant the Most High instituted with our forefather Abraham: every man child circumcised at eight days old, and the servant born in the house or bought with money circumcised likewise and keeping the laws as well.
- When Abraham received the commandment he performed it, circumcising every male of his house the selfsame day; he showed the Lord by his actions that he believed. So the men in Joshua who had not been circumcised showed a form of repentance by applying the law of circumcision.

  Precepts:
  - **[Genesis 17:10-12](/bible/genesis/17#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/genesis/17#v10)</sup> This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you and thy seed after thee; Every man child among you shall be circumcised.
    >
    > <sup>[11](/bible/genesis/17#v11)</sup> And ye shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a token of the covenant betwixt me and you.
    >
    > <sup>[12](/bible/genesis/17#v12)</sup> And he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every man child in your generations, he that is born in the house, or bought with money of any stranger, which is not of thy seed.

    The covenant with Abraham and his seed: every man child among you shall be circumcised, he that is eight days old, including the servant bought with money.
  - **[Genesis 17:23-24](/bible/genesis/17#v23)**
    > <sup>[23](/bible/genesis/17#v23)</sup> And Abraham took Ishmael his son, and all that were born in his house, and all that were bought with his money, every male among the men of Abraham’s house; and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin in the selfsame day, as God had said unto him.
    >
    > <sup>[24](/bible/genesis/17#v24)</sup> And Abraham was ninety years old and nine, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.

    Abraham circumcised every male of his house in the selfsame day, as God had said unto him; faith shown by doing.

- The eighth day is the wisdom of the Most High for the body: before then a baby's blood has not begun to coagulate as it needs to, and the child could bleed out; by the eighth day he is strong enough to withstand the process and heal.
- There are physical benefits to the law: when the foreskin remains, moisture gets trapped and creates an environment for bacteria, raising the risk of infection and urinary tract infections, and being circumcised even reduces a wife's risk of cervical cancer. This is the Most High as a Father giving his children counsel on how to live and stay clear of disease.
- The physical circumcision is symbolic of spiritual circumcision. The heart in scripture is the mind, for out of the heart of men proceed evil thoughts; sin is what makes a man dirty, nasty, and filthy, so the uncircumcised heart is the mind that will not keep the commandments.
- No surgery can circumcise the brain: circumcision of the heart is repentance. You wash you and make you clean by ceasing to do evil, and a young man cleanses his way by taking heed thereto according to the word of the Most High.

  Precepts:
  - **[Leviticus 26:41](/bible/leviticus/26#v41)**
    > <sup>[41](/bible/leviticus/26#v41)</sup> And that I also have walked contrary unto them, and have brought them into the land of their enemies; if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity:

    If then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they accept the punishment of their iniquity; the Lord speaks here of the heart, not the flesh.
  - **[Mark 7:21](/bible/mark/7#v21)**
    > <sup>[21](/bible/mark/7#v21)</sup> For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,

    From within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts; the heart is the mind.
  - **[Isaiah 1:16](/bible/isaiah/1#v16)**
    > <sup>[16](/bible/isaiah/1#v16)</sup> Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil;

    Wash you, make you clean; cease to do evil is how you are made clean.
  - **[Psalms 119:9](/bible/psalms/119#v9)**
    > <sup>[9](/bible/psalms/119#v9)</sup> Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.

    A young man cleanses his way by taking heed thereto according to thy word.

**[Joshua 5:4-6](/bible/joshua/5#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/joshua/5#v4)</sup> And this is the cause why Joshua did circumcise: All the people that came out of Egypt, that were males, even all the men of war, died in the wilderness by the way, after they came out of Egypt.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/joshua/5#v5)</sup> Now all the people that came out were circumcised: but all the people that were born in the wilderness by the way as they came forth out of Egypt, them they had not circumcised.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/joshua/5#v6)</sup> For the children of Israel walked forty years in the wilderness, till all the people that were men of war, which came out of Egypt, were consumed, because they obeyed not the voice of the Lord: unto whom the Lord sware that he would not shew them the land, which the Lord sware unto their fathers that he would give us, a land that floweth with milk and honey.

- This is the cause of the circumcision: all the men of war that came out of Egypt died in the wilderness because they obeyed not the voice of the Lord, and the generation born by the way had not been circumcised.
- That they had not circumcised themselves means they did not obey the voice of the Lord: they should have been circumcised physically and also mentally and spiritually.
- The land that floweth with milk and honey is understood by the Bible's own dictionary, precept upon precept: the rebels in Numbers called Egypt the land flowing with milk and honey, and Israel was brought out of the land of Egypt, so the phrase describes a land abundant in food. The milk goes into your cattle and your meats, and the honey goes into your vegetation.
- The mixed multitude and the children of Israel wept for the fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic they ate in Egypt: they were comfortable in their oppression and did not understand they were not free, the same mindset among our people in captivity today who say they are free and living their best life.
- The honey teaching carries a dietary lesson: hast thou found honey, eat so much as is sufficient for thee. Do not overeat; balance your salts, sugars, meats, and dainties moderately.

  Precepts:
  - **[Numbers 16:13](/bible/numbers/16#v13)**
    > <sup>[13](/bible/numbers/16#v13)</sup> Is it a small thing that thou hast brought us up out of a land that floweth with milk and honey, to kill us in the wilderness, except thou make thyself altogether a prince over us?

    The rebels called the land Israel came out of a land that floweth with milk and honey; that land was Egypt.
  - **[Exodus 20:2](/bible/exodus/20#v2)**
    > <sup>[2](/bible/exodus/20#v2)</sup> I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

    I am the Lord thy God which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
  - **[Numbers 11:4-5](/bible/numbers/11#v4)**
    > <sup>[4](/bible/numbers/11#v4)</sup> And the mixt multitude that was among them fell a lusting: and the children of Israel also wept again, and said, Who shall give us flesh to eat?
    >
    > <sup>[5](/bible/numbers/11#v5)</sup> We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick:

    The mixed multitude fell a lusting, and Israel wept for the fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic of Egypt; comfortable in their oppression.
  - **[Proverbs 25:16](/bible/proverbs/25#v16)**
    > <sup>[16](/bible/proverbs/25#v16)</sup> Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.

    Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee; the honey goes into your food, and the lesson is moderation.

**[Joshua 5:7](/bible/joshua/5#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/joshua/5#v7)</sup> And their children, whom he raised up in their stead, them Joshua circumcised: for they were uncircumcised, because they had not circumcised them by the way.

- Their children raised up in their stead Joshua circumcised, for they had not circumcised them by the way.
- A father can have his son circumcised in the flesh yet never circumcise him from the heart: if he never teaches him the laws and to obey the voice of the Lord, the physical circumcision alone profits him nothing. It is symbolic of obeying the voice of the Lord.

**[Joshua 5:8](/bible/joshua/5#v8)**

> <sup>[8](/bible/joshua/5#v8)</sup> And it came to pass, when they had done circumcising all the people, that they abode in their places in the camp, till they were whole.

- They abode in their places in the camp till they were whole: these were grown men, not eight day old babies, so they had to remain in the camp until they healed from the circumcision.

**[Joshua 5:9](/bible/joshua/5#v9)**

> <sup>[9](/bible/joshua/5#v9)</sup> And the Lord said unto Joshua, This day have I rolled away the reproach of Egypt from off you. Wherefore the name of the place is called Gilgal unto this day.

- This day have I rolled away the reproach of Egypt from off you: they finally believed and obeyed, circumcising themselves and obeying the voice of the Lord, so they were no longer a reproach, an embarrassment, or a disgrace.
- The children of Israel finally sanctified themselves, and the name of the place is called Gilgal unto this day.

**[Joshua 5:10-12](/bible/joshua/5#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/joshua/5#v10)</sup> And the children of Israel encamped in Gilgal, and kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the month at even in the plains of Jericho.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/joshua/5#v11)</sup> And they did eat of the old corn of the land on the morrow after the passover, unleavened cakes, and parched corn in the selfsame day.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/joshua/5#v12)</sup> And the manna ceased on the morrow after they had eaten of the old corn of the land; neither had the children of Israel manna any more; but they did eat of the fruit of the land of Canaan that year.

- The children of Israel encamped in Gilgal and kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the month at even in the plains of Jericho; the passover was instituted by the Most High, and you can read about it in [Exodus 12](/bible/exodus/12).
- They did eat of the old corn of the land on the morrow after the passover, and the manna ceased; the children of Israel had manna no more, but ate of the fruit of the land of Canaan that year.

**[Joshua 5:13-14](/bible/joshua/5#v13)**

> <sup>[13](/bible/joshua/5#v13)</sup> And it came to pass, when Joshua was by Jericho, that he lifted up his eyes and looked, and, behold, there stood a man over against him with his sword drawn in his hand: and Joshua went unto him, and said unto him, Art thou for us, or for our adversaries?
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/joshua/5#v14)</sup> And he said, Nay; but as captain of the host of the Lord am I now come. And Joshua fell on his face to the earth, and did worship, and said unto him, What saith my lord unto his servant?

- Joshua lifted up his eyes by Jericho and saw a man standing over against him with his sword drawn, a warrior. Joshua did not run; he went straight to him and asked, Art thou for us, or for our adversaries? There was no fear in the heart of Joshua.
- The man answered, Nay; but as captain of the host of the Lord am I now come. Host means army: he is the captain, the leader, of the army of the Lord.
- When Joshua realized who stood before him, the fear came: he fell on his face to the earth and did worship, and the leader of Israel's army called himself a servant, saying, What saith my lord unto his servant? Joshua had cleaved to Moses and understood who the captain of the host is.
- The captain of the host of the Lord is Christ, the captain of our salvation. This is why Joshua was afraid: the return of Christ is not the soft picture Christianity paints, for he is not coming back made like unto his brethren as at the first, but with the power of the living God, to take vengeance and destroy. No missiles or fighter jets will do anything against him.

  Precepts:
  - **[Hebrews 2:9-10](/bible/hebrews/2#v9)**
    > <sup>[9](/bible/hebrews/2#v9)</sup> But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.
    >
    > <sup>[10](/bible/hebrews/2#v10)</sup> For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.

    We see Jesus, made perfect through sufferings, the captain of their salvation; Christ is the captain of the host.
  - **[Isaiah 47:3](/bible/isaiah/47#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/isaiah/47#v3)</sup> Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen: I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.

    I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man; at his second coming Christ comes with the power of the living God.
  - **[Exodus 15:3](/bible/exodus/15#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/exodus/15#v3)</sup> The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.

    The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.

**[Joshua 5:15](/bible/joshua/5#v15)**

> <sup>[15](/bible/joshua/5#v15)</sup> And the captain of the Lord’s host said unto Joshua, Loose thy shoe from off thy foot; for the place whereon thou standest is holy. And Joshua did so.

- The captain of the Lord's host said, Loose thy shoe from off thy foot; for the place whereon thou standest is holy. And Joshua did so.
